caption_hook: 🐘 A Zambia elephant orphanage that began with 3 calves has now returned 20 orphans to the wild + 3 more wins you missed 👇
question: Which would you share first: 1, 2, 3 or 4?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves elephants
first_comment: Rachael Murton, who helped found the orphanage in 2008 and lived in a tent at first, just won IFAW's Wildlife Rescue Award. What animal would you want to help? 🐘

stories.headline: An elephant orphanage that began with 3 calves freed 20
stories.summary: Zambia's Elephant Orphanage Project started in 2008 with 3 calves. It has now released 20 orphans into the wild, more than the 17 still in care, a first in its history.
stories.why: Chamilandu, orphaned by poachers, gave birth to her 2nd calf in the wild last year, with no human help.

stories.stat_label: feeding black holes in one galaxy
stories.headline: 3 giant black holes were caught feeding in 1 ancient galaxy
stories.summary: In a galaxy seen just 1.2 billion years after the Big Bang, astronomers found 3 actively growing supermassive black holes. 2 of them sit only 620 light-years apart.
stories.why: They may one day merge, giving future gravitational-wave observatories a signal to catch.

stories.stat_label: body lengths a minute at top speed
stories.headline: MIT built a gum-sized robot that swims on living muscle
stories.summary: Its thin gel body has 2 fins coated in muscle cells that contract when lit. By steering the light, the team guided it through a small underwater maze.
stories.why: Soft robots that can heal themselves could one day explore fragile places that rigid machines would damage.

stories.headline: A rescued NZ forest is drawing flocks of native pigeons
stories.summary: Since 2017, volunteers at Staveley Camp have pulled out hundreds of invasive trees. Native plants are regrowing, and kererū counts rose from 2 or 3 birds for 6 years to 7 in 2025.
stories.why: It shows that caring for old forest patches can pay off, with schools and locals pitching in.

fun_fact: Elephants walk so quietly that, as the orphanage's co-founder says, they can appear right beside you unnoticed.
